title: Unsupervised learning reveals mixed-frequency seismic precursors before Axial Seamount’s 2015 eruption
summary: An analysis of four months of Axial Seamount seismicity combined supervised event discrimination with unsupervised spectral clustering and found a mixed-frequency earthquake class whose counts rose rapidly about 15 hours before the 2015 eruption. The events migrated along mapped eruptive fissures; the authors interpret them as brittle crack opening associated with magma or volatile influx. This is a retrospective single-eruption finding, not an operationally validated forecast.
ai_technology: Unsupervised machine-learning spectral clustering, with supervised event discrimination
organization: Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory, Columbia University; University of Washington; Chinese University of Hong Kong

evidence.tested: An analysis of four months of Axial Seamount seismicity combined supervised event discrimination with unsupervised spectral clustering and found a mixed-frequency earthquake class whose counts rose rapidly about 15 hours before the 2015 eruption.
evidence.unknown: The result is retrospective and concerns a single 2015 eruption at one well-instrumented submarine volcano. The proposed crack-opening/magma-or-volatile explanation is the authors’ interpretation; applicability to future eruptions or other volcanoes remains untested.
evidence.ai_role: Discriminated volcanic earthquakes from other signal sources and clustered waveform spectral features, revealing a previously unrecognized mixed-frequency event pattern and its timing and migration before eruption.
